description.p: Blockwork lets you build keyboard and mouse macros by snapping blocks together, without writing any code. Record your input and turn it into editable blocks, or assemble a sequence by hand, then play it back with a global hotkey.

ul.li: Record keyboard and mouse input, including mouse movement
Loops, If / If-Else blocks, variables, and operators
Reusable custom blocks with custom colors
Global hotkeys to start and stop macros

description.p: **Recording input and hotkeys requires your user to be in the input group. See the Help link for setup steps.**

screenshot.caption: Building a macro in the block editor

description.p: The project has moved to the Blockworked organization on GitHub.
Blockwork can now update itself on macOS.
Custom blocks were reworked and can now be given their own colors. The sidebar shows the correct operator type.
The app is now called Blockwork, with a new logo and a smoother block editor with better pan, zoom, and dragging.

ul.li: Loops, booleans, and If / If-Else blocks
Time and date blocks, app open and quit blocks, and a battery event

description.p: Macros are now built in a Scratch-like block editor. Variables show a live preview of their value, and new operators include Join, Random, and text blocks.
Hotkeys no longer stop working after switching windows with Alt+Tab.
Settings and macros are stored in a new config directory layout.
Global hotkeys can now be recorded, macros can be force-quit, and playback timing is more precise. Wait blocks accept fractional seconds and an optional random variance.
The run-script block can now run any command, and you are warned if your user is not in the input group.
Added input recording, custom hotkey settings, undo and redo, comments, and relative mouse movement. Large macros are faster to edit.
